rules.action: Scoring balloon first-line for moderate calcium.
rules.rationale: Scoring balloon disrupts calcium before stenting to improve expansion.
rules.detail: Escalate to IVL if a residual waist persists after scoring balloon inflation.

rules.action: Scoring or cutting balloon as first step; escalate to IVL before stenting if waist persists.
rules.rationale: Long moderately calcified lesions have higher risk of incomplete expansion across the stented segment.
rules.detail: Do not proceed to stenting with a persistent non-compliant balloon waist — escalate to IVL before definitive stenting.

rules.action: Plan calcium modification before the case. Confirm full balloon compliance before stenting.
rules.rationale: Severe calcium prevents adequate stent expansion and predicts stent underexpansion if not modified.
rules.detail: Short atherectomy bursts (<30s). Full balloon compliance (no residual waist) is required before stent deployment.

rules.action: Use intravascular imaging to assess calcium depth and distribution before selecting modification device.
rules.rationale: Calcium morphology determines efficacy of IVL vs RA — selecting without imaging risks inadequate preparation.
rules.detail: IVL preferred for deep/medial calcium, calcified nodules, large vessels (>3.5mm), aorto-ostial lesions where crossing is achievable. RA preferred for superficial calcium, diffuse long segments, balloon-uncrossable or undilatable lesions.

rules.action: RA followed by IVL (Dual-Prep) is a reasonable escalation when post-atherectomy imaging reveals persistent heavy calcification.
rules.rationale: DUAL-PREP registry demonstrated acceptable procedural success and complication rates with sequential RA+IVL. Previously considered contraindicated.
rules.detail: Indicated when single-device preparation is insufficient per intravascular imaging. Sequence: RA first → intravascular imaging → IVL if persistent heavy calcium.

rules.action: Plan calcium modification before the case. Short RA bursts (<30s) in long segments; consider staged debulking for diffuse disease.
rules.rationale: Long severely calcified lesions have compounding modification and deliverability challenges.
rules.detail: For RA in long segments: short bursts with low-speed technique and adequate flushing. Stage debulking if the segment is very diffuse — calcium modification at first sitting, stenting at second.

rules.action: IVL preferred over RA for ostial severe calcium.
rules.rationale: RA at the ostium risks guide catheter trauma during burr movement.
rules.detail: Disengage the guide during IVL pulses to avoid transmitting energy to the aortic root.
rules.caution: Do not inflate IVL balloon with guide deeply engaged at the ostium.

rules.action: Precise stent positioning is critical — use a short marker-to-marker stent where possible.
rules.rationale: Even a few millimetres of stent protrusion into the parent vessel causes significant flow disturbance.
rules.detail: Disengage the guide 1–2mm before final deployment to avoid crushing the proximal stent edge. Post-dilate with a non-compliant balloon flared at the ostium.

rules.action: Plan stent overlap zones carefully before deploying. Deploy distal stent first, work proximally.
rules.rationale: Unplanned overlap zones create unpredictable stent edges and geographic miss risk.
rules.detail: Post-dilate each segment with a non-compliant balloon before deploying the next stent. Intravascular imaging especially valuable here.
rules.caution: Avoid geographic miss at the proximal or distal edges — the risk of edge restenosis is high.

rules.action: Intravascular imaging mandatory before stenting to define true lesion extent and reference vessel diameter along the full length.
rules.rationale: Long segments (>30mm) frequently have variation in vessel size — single-point sizing underestimates or overestimates.
rules.detail: Deploy stents sequentially distal to proximal; plan overlap zones at ≥3mm. Post-dilate each segment before deploying the next. Geographic miss at either edge carries high restenosis risk.

rules.action: Restore antegrade flow before stenting where possible.
rules.rationale: Stenting without restoring flow risks undersizing (due to vessel collapse) and no-reflow on reperfusion.
rules.detail: Ensure full anticoagulation before wire manipulation. Staged approach (aspiration → reassess morphology → definitive stenting) reduces no-reflow risk in thrombus/acute occlusion.

rules.action: Staged approach: aspiration thrombectomy first to restore flow; reassess morphology before stenting.
rules.rationale: High thrombus burden overestimates lesion length and underestimates reference diameter — stenting without flow restoration leads to sizing errors and no-reflow.
rules.detail: If TIMI flow improves after aspiration, reassess true lesion before committing to stent sizing. If TIMI 0 persists after aspiration, consider pharmacoinvasive strategy (GPI infusion, deferred PCI at 24–48h).

rules.action: Aspiration thrombectomy recommended before balloon or stent delivery.
rules.rationale: Manual aspiration reduces distal embolisation and thrombus burden, improving TIMI flow and reducing no-reflow risk.
rules.detail: Most effective when thrombus is proximal and large; less effective in distal or small-vessel locations. If high residual thrombus burden persists after aspiration, consider deferred stenting (24–48h with anticoagulation and GPI) to allow resolution.

rules.action: Avoid aspiration thrombectomy. EPD mandatory. Consider pharmacoinvasive approach before definitive stenting.
rules.rationale: SVG occlusion with thrombus: friable degenerated plaque causes catastrophic embolisation with aspiration. EPD and GP IIb/IIIa before stenting reduces distal embolisation.
rules.detail: If proceeding, direct stenting preferable to pre-dilation to minimise embolisation from uncontrolled plaque displacement.
rules.caution: Aspiration thrombectomy in a thrombosed degenerated SVG carries high no-reflow risk — avoid unless the graft is clearly non-degenerated.

rules.action: Avoid aspiration thrombectomy. Use EPD as standard. Pre-treat with GP IIb/IIIa inhibitor.
rules.rationale: Degenerated vein grafts carry high friable plaque burden — aspiration significantly increases distal embolisation and no-reflow risk.
rules.detail: Consider direct stenting to trap thrombus rather than pre-dilation where anatomy permits. Slow, prolonged inflations at nominal pressures.

rules.action: Avoid balloon pre-dilatation unless the lesion is severely stenotic or EPD delivery requires it.
rules.rationale: Pre-dilation in degenerated grafts increases distal embolisation risk from uncontrolled plaque fracture.
rules.detail: Prefer direct stenting to trap friable plaque beneath stent struts. Slow, prolonged inflations at nominal pressures. Avoid post-dilatation where possible — if required, size 1:1 with the graft and never oversize.

rules.action: Consider EPD whenever technically feasible. Administer intracoronary vasodilators liberally — even before balloon or stenting.
rules.rationale: EPD reduces distal embolisation. Pre-emptive vasodilators (verapamil, adenosine, nitroprusside, nicardipine) prevent and treat no-reflow most effectively when delivered distally.
rules.detail: Most effective vasodilator delivery: via microcatheter or over-the-wire balloon positioned distally. When no-reflow occurs with EPD in situ, aspirate before filter retrieval.

rules.action: Heavy SVG thrombus burden: dedicated aspiration catheters, guide extension aspiration, or mechanical thrombectomy for very large thrombus.
rules.rationale: Significant intragreft thrombus increases no-reflow risk proportionally — reducing bulk before stenting improves outcomes.
rules.detail: Dedicated catheters (Pronto, Export) or guide extension (GuideLiner, Guidezilla) for moderate burden. Mechanical thrombectomy (AngioJet, Penumbra) for very large thrombus. Intragraft fibrinolytics (tPA) described anecdotally. Maintain high ACT throughout.
rules.caution: Limited RCT evidence — no large randomised trial data for SVG thrombectomy devices.

rules.action: Keep individual atherectomy bursts and balloon inflation times short (<30s). Have vasopressors immediately available.
rules.rationale: Prolonged balloon inflations in reduced EF may cause haemodynamic instability — the myocardium has minimal reserve.
rules.detail: Brief the team before starting. Consider staged procedure: calcium modification at first sitting, stenting at second, if haemodynamic reserve is borderline.

rules.action: Keep inflation times short; deflate promptly if haemodynamics deteriorate. Consider staged procedure.
rules.rationale: Large territory at risk during balloon inflations in reduced EF — limited haemodynamic tolerance for extended ischaemia.
rules.detail: Staged strategy: lesion modification at first sitting, definitive stenting at second.

rules.action: Calcium modification must achieve full lesion compliance before stenting. Accept a longer procedure.
rules.rationale: A stent that fails to expand fully in the only remaining coronary is a catastrophic result. Do not rush lesion preparation.
rules.caution: Do not stent until full balloon compliance is confirmed — there is no bailout if the result is inadequate.

rules.action: Pre-dilate cautiously with vasopressors immediately available. For LM shaft or ostial disease without bifurcation, a single stent is preferred.
rules.rationale: LM pre-dilation can cause acute haemodynamic instability — partial occlusion during inflation compromises total cardiac output.
rules.detail: IVUS-guided stent sizing mandatory. For LM bifurcation, provisional strategy preferred unless large SB (>2.5mm) with true ostial disease. Ensure continuous haemodynamic monitoring throughout.
